https://www.birminghammail.co.uk/news/mi.text: A Birmingham man left a female police officer with cuts and bruising when he attacked her after a row broke out over his tenancy. Mitu Lucan, 60, assaulted two officers, spitting at one, during the scuffle as they dragged him out of his Wattville Road home in Handsworth on April 22 this year. But his defence lawyer told a Birmingham court he had simply reacted to people causing a commotion at the home, and that him refusing to leave his own home, was "not a reason to arrest someone". READ MORE: Sneaky 'crisp trick' Birmingham Tesco thief used to steal whiskey worth thousands Lucan, of Wattville Road , was sentenced to an 18-month community order after pleading guilty at an earlier hearing in May. He was also ordered to complete 20 Rehabilitation Activity Requirement days and 150 hours of unpaid work. Police attended Lucan's address following reports of "fighting" and a "commotion" - with Lucan said to have been upset over people in the building he felt shouldn't be there. Birmingham Magistrates' Court heard how, when officers arrived, they tried to "reason" with Lucan and asked him to leave the property, but he refused. At Lucan's sentencing on Monday (September 28), the court heard how the Romanian national called officers "crazy" and began waving around "his tenancy agreement". Shajah Javed, prosecuting, said: "Police were called to reports of fighting at the property. Officers tried to reason with the defendant and told him to leave. "He refused and stayed inside his address. He called officers 'crazy' and began showing them his tenancy agreement." Mr Javed said, when Lucan resisted arrest, he "had a scuffle" with a male officer. This led to a female officer trying to intervene which left her with "cuts and bruising to her hands" from Lucan attacking her, Mr Javed said. "He also grabbed hold of her stab vest," Mr Javed added. "During the arrest he began spitting at the male officer." Lucan was subsequently charged with two counts of assaulting a constable in the execution of his/her duty. His defence solicitor argued Lucan had simply reacted to people causing commotion at his address and said, him refusing to leave his own home was "not a reason to arrest someone". The court heard how Lucan, who had been drinking alcohol before his arrest, had tried to "explain" he lived there but "officers weren't having any of it". Lucan pleaded guilty at an earlier hearing in May. Magistrate Ms Hake JP said the sentence was reflected by Lucan assaulting police officers when they were "going about their business in the line of duty". "We have taken into consideration your early guilty plea but this was heightened because of the assault on officers," said the magistrate during her sentencing. Lucan was also told to pay £201 in court costs.
